{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjqe88AAAABZhMXPQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3INzhDINEw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IN", "number": 105, "title": "Add an evidence-qualified browser-local Archie filename and location search journey", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `8c258b0c0a619360612889dacbeabb6a0e943327`, MAIN or index → `7` offers NetNews, TELNET, FTP and Gopher, but no Archie experience. Users cannot search filenames and discover their archive locations, a distinct period activity supported by contemporary capability reporting.

This extends the service coverage deliberately deferred by Issue #103; it is not a demonstrated regression. PC-VAN's original Archie access route and controls remain unresolved.

## Expected outcome

Add `5 Archie` to the Internet directory, preserving selectors 1–4 and MAIN mappings. Provide a complete keyboard journey: Internet directory → Archie query view → filename lookup → matching locations or honest zero results → replacement query → return through the actual MAIN/index parent.

Use a small original, bundled index available anonymously without AI consent or model loading. Keep lookup separate from file acquisition.

## Context

### Historical evidence and reconstruction judgment

Sources inspected on 2026-10-24:

- [Internet White Paper 1996, printed p.111](https://iwparchives.jp/files/pdf/iwp1996/iwp1996-ch04-01-p110.pdf): its comparison labeled January 1996 marks Archie available for PC-VAN, separately identifies graphical clients and restricts FTP to info.mac. Moderate-to-high confidence in the extracted capability table. It establishes neither text-host access nor commands. Later planned changes also appear, so the table label is not an activation date. No usable page-image comparison was obtained.
- [Internet Magazine, January 1996, printed p.229](https://iwparchives.jp/wp-content/themes/twentytwelve/bn/pdf/im199601-216-news.pdf): the Navigator/Mosaic review describes restrictions on choosing Internet software and Archie servers in that environment. High confidence in the inspected passage; its client context cannot establish a service-wide prohibition or November behavior.
- [RFC 1580, March 1994, section 5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1580.html): documents filename/location lookup, separate access methods, PROG results with host, directory, size and modification date, and several matching modes. Exact matching is the documented default; case-insensitive substring matching is an available mode. High confidence in these general Archie semantics, without PC-VAN-specific authentication.

Accept category D reconstruction for Internet selector 5, Japanese presentation, local navigation controls, index contents, ordering and a single case-insensitive literal filename-substring mode. Choose `PROG <filename fragment>` as a disclosed local control inspired by general Archie documentation, never as authenticated PC-VAN syntax. Its matching rule intentionally differs from the RFC's documented default. Carrying reported capability into the fictional late-1996 setting is a moderate-confidence continuity assumption.

Focused searches produced no qualifying PC-VAN host sequence. Earlier cross-provider examples and a search-only announcement in an inaccessible later discussion archive do not supply implementation commands. The access-route uncertainty remains open and does not prevent this explicitly qualified subset.

### Implementation and existing evidence

`src/netnews.ts::renderInternetDirectory` and `src/navigation.ts` expose four services. `src/gopher.ts` provides a small visit-local precedent. Inspect `src/commands.ts`, `src/connection.ts` and `src/main.ts` together: command ownership must prevent generic composition interception, controller state needs forwarding, and successful restore must invalidate the visit. These are integration points, not a requirement for a new abstraction or storage system.

[PR #104](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/pull/104) and `docs/validation.md` report 375 passing checks with three workers, including configured type checking/build, after disclosed test corrections. This graph inspected those records and ran no application checks. Default/eight-worker reliability remains unresolved.

Live repository searches returned no open Issues or PRs. The Archie history search found [Issue #103](https://github.com/takahirox/pcvan/issues/103), whose Gopher scope explicitly excludes Archie. Searches are terminology-dependent and inventory can change.

## Pre-merge acceptance

1. **Bounded lookup service.** Add `5 Archie` from both MAIN → 7 and index → 7. Bundle at least three original index rows covering at least two filenames, including one filename at two distinct locations. Use fictional `.invalid` hosts, original directory paths, illustrative byte sizes and modification dates appropriate to the selected period. Label these as authored examples; import no historical files, identities, messages or screenshots.

2. **Filename semantics.** Accept `PROG <filename fragment>` in the query and results views. Match only the filename field using deterministic case-insensitive literal substring matching. Trim outer query whitespace, preserve internal whitespace and display the submitted query literally. Do not search hostnames, directory paths, descriptions, metadata or document bodies. Empty/malformed input preserves the current state with useful guidance. Regex/Boolean-looking text is literal. Results show the query, location count and each matching filename, host, directory, size and modification date. Count distinct locations separately; unmatched queries produce zero results.

3. **Predictable navigation.** `HELP` and `LIST` redisplay the current view. Replacement queries replace results without accumulating return frames. From results, `BACK` returns to the query view; further returns reach the Internet directory and actual MAIN/index parent. `MAIN` and fresh entry clear previous queries/results. Results are informational locations, with no selection, download or automatic FTP handoff. Preserve existing restricted FTP behavior.

4. **Isolation and lifecycle.** Reject unsupported selectors and unrelated forum, mail, OLT, conference, Gopher, TELNET, FTP, BiZ, composition and acquisition commands contextually. Preserve modern application-control ownership, Settings/About context and unsent input, IME guards, terminal scrolling/logging and normal disconnect/reconnect. Cancelled restore/reset retains the visit; successful same-tab/cross-tab restore and reset follow existing invalidation safeguards. Add no transport, endpoint entry, network lookup, persistence/schema fields, worker or model work. Ordinary session/history recording may continue.

5. **Evidence disclosure.** Update README, the existing historical research document and discoverable About content with source URLs, access dates, historical scope, confidence, original authorship, category D decisions and unresolved host/client access. Explicitly distinguish the chosen substring mode from the documented general default. Brief routine guidance should identify the bundled local example; do not claim live indexing, authenticated PC-VAN commands, complete coverage or protocol conformance. Keep host paging, graphical clients and other MAIN destinations outside this Issue.

6. **Focused Coordinator checks using existing tooling.** Add controller and production Playwright coverage for both entry parents; duplicate-location results and metadata; mixed-case matching; filename-only negative controls; literal punctuation and internal whitespace; Japanese/markup query rendering; malformed input; replacement/zero-result queries; return paths; MAIN/re-entry; command isolation; connection forwarding; Settings/About; synthetic IME; and restore/reset lifecycle behavior. Exercise an anonymous restored-empty world and a registered world, including a 320px keyboard journey. Compare protected members/SIGs/forums/posts/mail/read-state/settings and JSON exports before/after, allowing normal session/history changes. Confirm the index never seeds imported records or enters backups, and browsing with AI disabled introduces no external/model requests, workers, popups or downloads. Explicit backup/log exports remain available.

7. **Preserve existing coverage and report actual results.** Run relevant existing Internet/navigation, functional, storage, consent, composition, IME and terminal checks, then `npm test -- --workers=3`; the existing configuration includes TypeScript checking and production build. Record commands, outcomes, failures, corrections and skipped checks. Preserve behavioral assertions; update only expectations legitimately affected by selector 5. Review the final diff, documentation links/anchors and `git diff --check`. Do not report three-worker success as resolving default-worker reliability.

## Optional validation

Native Japanese IME, additional browser engines and historical-user feedback may supplement automated evidence. None is a completion gate. No real-model or hardware validation is needed.

## Required post-merge verification

None required. Record the Coordinator's pre-merge evidence; no separate post-merge test or deployment verification is required.
